identity_mapping.description: Maps the user identifier from Segment/RudderStack events to Heap's identity field. Heap requires a single string identity per user, resolved from userId. If userId is absent, anonymousId is used as fallback. The identity value is case-sensitive and limited to 255 characters.

mappings.notes: Primary identity resolution. Heap identity is a case-sensitive string, max 255 characters. If userId is present, it is used directly as the Heap identity.
Fallback identity when userId is not available. Used for anonymous visitor tracking before identification.

event_property_mapping.description: Maps event properties from Segment/RudderStack track calls to Heap event properties. All custom properties are passed through directly. Heap property keys must be under 512 characters; values must be scalar types (string, number, boolean) or arrays, with string values under 1024 characters.

mappings.notes: Event name mapped directly. Heap event names are case-sensitive strings.
All custom event properties are passed through as-is. Property keys must be < 512 chars, string values < 1024 chars. Supported types: string, number, boolean, array.
Library name from context is optionally appended to properties for attribution. Segment uses 'segment_library', RudderStack uses 'rudderstack_library'.
ISO 8601 timestamp of the event. Heap uses this to order events chronologically. Must be within the last 12 months.
Message ID mapped to Heap's idempotency_key for deduplication. Ensures the same event is not processed twice.

user_property_mapping.description: Maps user traits from Segment/RudderStack identify calls to Heap user properties via the /api/add_user_properties endpoint. All traits are sent as persistent user-level properties.

mappings.notes: All user traits from identify calls are mapped directly to Heap user properties. Properties persist on the user profile and can be used for filtering and segmentation in Heap.
Email trait mapped to Heap user property. Commonly used for user identification in Heap's UI.
Display name trait mapped to Heap user property.
Account creation date trait mapped to Heap user property for cohort analysis.

app_id_config.description: Heap uses the app_id field in every API request body for authentication and project identification. The app_id is a numeric string obtained from the Heap project settings and must be configured as a destination setting in RudderStack/Segment. Unlike most destinations, Heap does not use an Authorization header; authentication is exclusively through the app_id in the JSON body.

mappings.notes: The Heap app_id is injected from the destination configuration into every API request body. This is the sole authentication mechanism for the Heap Server-Side API. The value is a numeric string (e.g., '4111348877') found in Heap Project Settings > Environment.

required_settings.name: appId
required_settings.description: Heap Environment App ID. A numeric string found in Heap project settings under Account > Manage > Environment. This is the primary authentication credential for the Heap Server-Side API and is included in every API request body.

optional_settings.name: useAnonymousIdAsIdentity
optional_settings.description: When enabled, uses anonymousId as the Heap identity when userId is not present. When disabled, events without userId are dropped.

optional_settings.name: appendLibraryToProperties
optional_settings.description: When enabled, appends the SDK library name (e.g., 'rudder-sdk-js') as a property on track events for attribution tracking.

track.notes: Track events map one-to-one between Segment and RudderStack to Heap's /api/track endpoint. Event name, properties, timestamp, and identity are mapped identically. The only difference is the SDK library name appended to properties (analytics.js vs rudder-sdk-js) and envelope metadata fields.

identify.notes: Identify events map one-to-one between Segment and RudderStack to Heap's /api/add_user_properties endpoint. All user traits are sent as Heap user properties. Identity resolution uses the same userId-first, anonymousId-fallback strategy.

known_gaps.impact: Heap supports account-level properties via /api/add_account_properties, which requires a Segment group call. Neither Segment nor RudderStack currently map group calls to Heap's account properties API in the cloud-mode Heap integration.
known_gaps.workaround: Use Heap's Account Tracking feature with client-side SDK or custom server-side integration.

known_gaps.impact: Heap provides a /api/batch_track endpoint supporting up to 1000 events per request for higher throughput. Neither Segment nor RudderStack cloud-mode integrations utilize the batch endpoint; events are sent individually.
known_gaps.workaround: Individual event delivery is reliable and within Heap's rate limits (30 req/30s per identity). Batch support can be added as a future optimization.

known_gaps.impact: Heap enforces 30 requests per 30 seconds per identity per app_id. RudderStack's Router-level retry and throttling behavior may differ slightly from Segment's retry strategy when rate limits are hit.
known_gaps.workaround: RudderStack Router has built-in retry with exponential backoff that handles 429 responses gracefully.

recommended_validation: Verify app_id is correctly injected from destination config into every API request body
Confirm identity resolution: userId used when present, anonymousId as fallback
Validate event properties pass-through with correct types (string, number, boolean, array)
Test identify call maps all traits to user properties via /api/add_user_properties
Verify timestamp format is ISO 8601 and within Heap's 12-month window
Confirm idempotency_key is populated from messageId for deduplication
Test rate limit handling: 429 responses trigger retry with backoff
Validate property key length < 512 chars and string value length < 1024 chars

notes: Heap shared cloud destination. Category: Analytics. Heap is a digital insights platform for product analytics. The Heap Server-Side API uses /api/track for event tracking and /api/add_user_properties for user trait persistence. Authentication is via app_id in the request body (no Authorization header). Rate limited to 30 requests per 30 seconds per identity per app_id. Segment slug: actions-heap. Priority: P2 in destination gap analysis. Supports track and identify event types for cloud-mode delivery.
